title: World Literacy Over Two Centuries
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Predict the world's literacy rate in 1820, when more than half the world first became literate, and what share of adults still cannot read, then see each answer on a line chart from 1820 to 2024.

learningObjectives: Interpret a line chart of the share of the world's people who could read from 1820 to today, answering at least 2 of 3 prediction questions correctly before each answer is revealed.
prerequisites: The UNESCO estimate of adults who cannot read

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then reveal (prediction questions with data feedback), followed by free exploration
keyQuestions: How many people could read two hundred years ago?
When did more than half the world first become literate?
Is illiteracy now too rare to matter?
commonMisconceptions: Most people have been able to read since the invention of printing.
Mass literacy is centuries old in most of the world.
Illiteracy is now so rare it no longer matters.
assessmentOpportunities: Score on three locked-in predictions (mastery: 2 of 3).
Explain why a small share of illiterate adults is still a large number of people.

dataSources.name: Our World in Data, Literate and illiterate world population (World series)
UNESCO estimate of adults lacking basic literacy (about 750 million)
UN World Population Prospects 2024 (about 6.1 billion adults aged 15+, approximate)
